overall: The AG found the Board may no longer withhold most of its October 3, 2023 executive session minutes now that the litigation is settled, except the settlement-capacity portion; the minutes were also insufficient and must be amended and released.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly withheld minutes of its October 3, 2023 executive session after the related litigation settled and was dismissed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the litigation matter discussed in executive session on October 3, 2023, has concluded, the executive session purpose has been served, and the Board may no longer rely on the Open Meeting Law to withhold the minutes other than that portion of the minutes that records the Town’s settlement capacity.

allegations.summary: Board claimed it could keep withholding the minutes portion recording the Town's maximum settlement authority because release could harm its future litigating position.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board may rely on the Open Meeting Law to continue to withhold that portion of the minutes of the October 3 executive session that record discussion of the Town’s maximum settlement authority where release of such information could have a detrimental effect on the Board’s litigating position in the future.

allegations.summary: Board asserted the minutes were protected by attorney-client privilege and could be withheld on that basis.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Open Meeting Law does not authorize the Attorney General to determine whether the Board’s assertion of the attorney-client privilege is justified.

allegations.summary: Although not raised by complainant, the AG reviewed the October 3, 2023 executive session minutes in camera and found them too brief to summarize the discussion.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 60 days, amend the October 3, 2023 executive session minutes to substantively summarize the discussions held and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
Release the amended October 3, 2023 executive session minutes to the public, subject to appropriate redactions under the attorney-client privilege or Public Records Law exemptions.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law.
